NORTH-CHINA SUNDAY NEWS, FEBRUARY 22, 1931    39
& S. REC.
S. B. D. 2121.
10 - 3 - 31

CHINESE PEOPLE'S
LIVELIHOOD

N.C.C. Conference Opening in
Shanghai To-day

The Conference on the "People's
Livelihood" which is being conven-
ed by the National Christian Coun-
cil will hold its opening meeting
this afternoon at 3 p.m. in the Chi-
nese Y.M.C.A., 201 Szechuen Road.
Dr. H. H. Kung, who is honorary
chairman of the Conference will be
present to open the Conference. This
meeting is for Conference-members
only. Those desiring to attend
should apply for tickets at the
Chinese Y.M.C.A.

Delegates from the major cities
of China have already arrived, and
indicate that a wide range of ex-
perience will be brought to bear in
the discussions. Among those
from the North are Professor L. K.
Tao of the Social Research Insti-
tute of the China Foundation. Under
his guidance there has recently been
published what is probably the most
soundly based study of the Standard
of living of workers in Shanghai
which has yet appeared. It is
based on the family budgets kept
daily over a period of a year in-
volving some 250 families: and this,
though not too small a number for
a scientific sample, is a great
achievement under the circum-
stances. From Peking come also
Professor Gireon Chen and Dr.
Jefferson Lamb.

From Shantung there comes Mr.
W. B. Djang of the Christian Liter-
acy Board, Tsingchow, to partici-
pate in the discussions on Workers'
Education. From Wuhan and from
Szechuan men of experience in
social and economic issues have
arrived. Mr. Kao, of the Mass
Education College of the Kiangsu
Provincial Government, will give
one of the evening addresses upon
the Wusih experiments. Miss Dju
Yu Bao, the first industrial welfare
worker of scientific training at work
in a silk filature in Wusih, has also
arrived. Government officials from
Nanking and Shanghai, research
students, social workers: Mr. C. C.
Chang from the statistical section
of the Legislative Yuan whose
wide experience in rural economics
in this country, and others ensure
in advance the quality of the dis-
cussions.

Professor R. H. Tawney to Speak

Following the opening greeting,
Professor R. H. Tawney will speak
at the Chinese Y.M.C.A. this after-
noon. He has been, during the
past three months, been making a
study into the agricultural economy
of China on behalf of the Institute
of Pacific Relations in preparation
for the Hangchow conference in
October. The address to-day will
be upon the general subject of the
conference. The remainder of the
conference will confine itself to
lectures, papers and discussions
based directly upon China material.
Details of the daily programmes
will be published and any who are
interested in participation in any
or all of the meetings are invited to
communicate with the secretary of
the conference, 38 Yuen Ming Yuen
Road. Morning sessions will be
held in Room 303, Yuen Ming
Yuen Road.

SI, the discussions at this conference
may be of interest.
J.H.S. 23:2:31

《华北星期新闻》，1931年2月22日    39
& S. REC.
S. B. D. 2121.
10 - 3 - 31

中国人民的
生计

中华全国基督教协进会会议
今日在上海开幕

由中华全国基督教协进会召集的“人民生计”会议，将于今日下午3时在四川路201号中华青年会举行开幕式。会议名誉主席孔祥熙博士将出席并宣布会议开幕。此次会议仅限会议代表参加。欲出席者应向中华青年会索取入场券。

来自中国各大城市的代表已经抵达，这表明讨论中将涵盖广泛的经验。来自北方的代表中有中华教育文化基金董事会社会调查部的陶履恭教授。在他的指导下，最近出版了迄今看来依据最为扎实的上海工人生活水准研究。该研究基于约250个家庭在一年期间每日记录的家庭收支账目；尽管对于一个科学样本而言，这一数量并非过小，但在当时情况下已是一项重大成就。来自北京的还有陈吉人教授和兰金生博士。

来自山东的是青州基督教识字运动委员会的张伯怀先生，他将参与关于工人教育的讨论。来自武汉和四川的具有社会及经济问题经验的人士也已抵达。江苏省政府民众教育学院的髙先生将就无锡实验发表晚间演讲之一。朱玉宝小姐是第一位在无锡丝厂工作的受过科学训练的工业福利工作者，她也已抵达。来自南京和上海的政府官员、研究生、社会工作者：立法院统计处的张心一先生，他在中国农村经济方面拥有丰富经验，以及其他人士，预先保证了讨论的质量。

R. H. 托尼教授将发表演讲

在开幕致辞之后，R. H. 托尼教授将于今日下午在中华青年会发表演讲。在过去的三个月里，他一直代表太平洋国际学会研究中国农业经济，为十月的杭州会议做准备。今日的演讲将围绕会议的一般主题展开。会议的其余部分将局限于直接基于中国材料的讲座、论文和讨论。每日日程详情将会公布，任何有兴趣参加部分或全部会议的人，请与圆明园路38号的会议秘书联系。上午的会议将在圆明园路303室举行。

SI，本次会议的讨论可能会引起兴趣。
